sections.h2: Which Nelson County office sets value and which sends the bill?
sections.html:
The sheriff sends bills and takes the money. The Property Valuation Administration (PVA), at (502) 348-1810, sets value. The sheriff's page says outright that the sheriff never assesses anything, so complaints about a figure belong at the PVA.

What lands in the mailbox depends on the district. The sheriff collects for the state, the county and school districts, and where a contract exists for cities and special districts as well.

  • Districts 1, 7, 8, 11, 12 and 13: county bill alone.
  • District 2: county plus the City of New Haven.
  • District 3: county schools plus the City of Bardstown.
  • District 4: county, Bardstown city and Bardstown Independent Schools.
  • District 5: county plus Bardstown Independent Schools.
  • District 9: county plus the City of Fairfield.

A house inside Bardstown can generate several bills, so a seller should gather all of them before asking for a payoff.

sections.h2: What is Nelson County like for a house sale?
sections.html:
Nelson County became the fourth Kentucky county in 1784, carved from Jefferson County. It spans about 418 square miles of land. Bardstown, the seat, ranks among the state's oldest cities and counted 13,567 people in 2020. The area calls itself the Bourbon Capital of the World, and Heaven Hill, Barton 1792, Willett and Lux Row operate in and near town.

The sheriff's patrol area runs through Bardstown, Bloomfield, New Haven, Fairfield, Boston, Chaplin and New Hope, so one county holds several distinct town markets. Bardstown grows around the crossing of U.S. 31E, U.S. 62 and U.S. 150, with the Bluegrass Parkway just to the south. Wikipedia places the county in the Louisville combined statistical area.

Bardstown City Schools and Nelson County Schools both operate here, and the Archdiocese of Louisville runs Catholic schools. Nelson County High School stands within the boundaries of the Bardstown district, so buyers should confirm the district for a specific address. Bardstown has a humid subtropical climate with hot summers, mild to cool winters and about 52 inches of precipitation a year, with roughly a foot of snow.

sections.h2: What does Census data say about Nelson County housing?
sections.html:
The population estimate for July 2025 is 49,036, up 4.9% from the 2020 base. Of residents 16 and older, 63.0% are in the labor force.

  • 21,097 housing units in 2025, with 222 building permits that year.
  • Owners occupy 78.3% of homes in 2020 to 2024.
  • The Census midpoint for an owned house is $238,000.
  • Monthly costs run $1,379 with a mortgage and $473 with none.
  • Gross rent has a midpoint of $1,008.
  • Household income has a midpoint of $69,562, and 11.7% of people are in poverty.

Around 90.3% of residents had not moved in the past year, and 23.8% of adults 25 and over hold a four-year degree. With 222 permits, resale listings compete with newly built homes.

sections.h2: Which Nelson County and Bardstown features draw buyers?
sections.html:
The bourbon industry shows in the economy. The Census Bureau counts 1,023 employer establishments for 2023 with total employment of 17,214 and a payroll of $926,774 thousand, and employment grew 3.8% from 2022. Retail sales for 2022 reached $836,642 thousand, about $17,666 per resident, and medical and social service providers took in $202,154 thousand.

Bardstown adds history to the draw. Its Old Talbott Tavern dates to 1779 and is described as the oldest western stagecoach stop still operating. A Bardstown historic district carries a federal historic register listing, and the Civil War Museum is described as the fourth largest in the country. My Old Kentucky Home State Park hosts The Stephen Foster Story each summer. The Basilica of St. Joseph Proto-Cathedral recalls the 1808 founding of the Diocese of Bardstown, the first Catholic diocese west of the Appalachians. Residents travel an average of 26.6 minutes to work, and the Kentucky Bourbon Festival, designated the state's official bourbon festival in 2000, draws visitors to town each year.

sections.h2: How do Nelson County penalties stack up over the season?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 gives the pattern, and the sheriff's page confirms the dates.

Nelson County Sheriff, what each payment date costs
If paidEffect on the bill
Up to November 1Two percent knocked off
Between November 2 and December 31Bill stands as printed
During JanuaryFive percent extra
February 1 through April 15Twenty-one percent extra

On a $2,500 bill the totals are $2,450, $2,500, $2,625 and $3,025, so a latecomer pays $575 more than an early payer. Anything unpaid at the sheriff by April 15 passes to the County Clerk.

The sheriff returns any check that differs from the bill by even a dollar, as well as late or partial ones, because audit rules demand exact accounting. If a lender escrows your tax, send the bill to the lender. The first proper payment received gets processed, and no refund goes to an owner who pays ahead of the lender.

sections.h2: How does a Nelson County owner challenge an assessment?
sections.html:
Begin at the PVA, which holds a conference with the owner or a representative. KRS 133.120 requires it before any formal appeal, and a phone call can count. The tax roll is displayed for 13 days beginning the opening Monday in May under KRS 133.045, and the conference must fall before or during that stretch.

A disagreement that survives the conference becomes a written petition at the County Clerk. It lists the parcel, the reasons and the owner's estimate, and it is due the workday after inspection closes. Hearings are public, and the owner supplies the facts: sales listings, insurance policies, construction costs or loan papers. The bill itself is not delayed, and an increase is billed with interest from the original due date.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for Kentucky's homestead exemption in Nelson County?
sections.html: Owners aged 65 and up, and owners classified as totally disabled, are eligible. The state figure of $49,100 applies to the 2025 and 2026 years. On a home assessed at the county midpoint of $238,000, taxes would be figured on $188,900. File with the Nelson County PVA with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport as proof of age. Disability claims renew each year, except for service-connected veterans and for owners ruled permanently and totally disabled by federal Social Security or the state retirement system.

sections.h2: What tax tasks should a Nelson County seller finish before closing?
sections.html:
The tax is a personal debt of the January 1 owner, and delinquent property carries a lien for eleven years under KRS 134.420. A buyer's title company searches for it.

  • Collect every bill for the parcel, including city and independent school lines for a Bardstown address.
  • Ask the sheriff for the exact payoff on the planned closing date.
  • Write the buyer's mailing address for tax bills into the deed, per KRS 382.135.
  • For an inherited house, the executor files an affidavit with the County Clerk naming recipients and values.

A New Haven or Bardstown city bill is separate from the county bill, so a payoff quoting only the county number leaves a gap.

faqs.q: Which office handles a Nelson County valuation complaint?
faqs.a: The PVA, at (502) 348-1810. The sheriff does not assess property.

faqs.q: Does the Nelson County Sheriff take inexact payments?
faqs.a: No. A check that does not match the bill exactly, along with any late or partial payment, is returned.

faqs.q: What becomes of a Nelson County bill still open after April 15?
faqs.a: It moves from the sheriff to the Nelson County Clerk.

faqs.q: Do bills differ across Nelson County?
faqs.a: Yes. Districts 1, 7, 8, 11, 12 and 13 get one county bill, while districts 2, 3, 4, 5 and 9 also receive New Haven, Bardstown, Bardstown Independent School or Fairfield bills.

faqs.q: What deduction does a senior get on a Nelson County home?
faqs.a: The state subtracts $49,100 from assessed value for 2025 and 2026, once an owner 65 or older, or totally disabled, applies at the PVA.
